subject: Media Literacy
title: Repetition and Brand Recall
description: A fast breakdown of Repetition and Brand Recall for builders.

hook.text: You can hum the McDonald's jingle right now. You've been hearing it since childhood.

buildup.text: Repetition is advertising's oldest weapon. Seeing a brand repeatedly makes it feel familiar and trustworthy.

discovery.text: The 'mere exposure effect' means we prefer things simply because we've seen them before.

twist.text: You think you chose that brand. Your brain just picked the one it recognized from 10,000 impressions.

climax.text: Brand loyalty often isn't loyalty. It's the accumulated effect of relentless repetition.

punchline.text: Familiarity isn't trust. It's just exposure.

quiz.question: What is the 'mere exposure effect'?
options: We avoid things we see too often
We prefer things simply because we've encountered them before
We remember the first ad we ever saw
